```{r}
#| label: summarize_steps
summary_qc = sets_qc_evaluation |>
  dplyr::select(completed_steps, failed_steps, failed_why) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    perc = n / 6103,
    .by = c(completed_steps, failed_steps, failed_why)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(completed_steps, failed_steps, failed_why)

n_completed = summary_qc |>
  dplyr::filter(completed_steps %in% "se; dynamic_range; correlation; pca") |>
  dplyr::pull(n)
perc_completed = summary_qc |>
  dplyr::filter(completed_steps %in% "se; dynamic_range; correlation; pca") |>
  dplyr::pull(perc)
perc_display = paste0(format(perc_completed * 100, digits = 2), "%")
```

## Introduction

Depositing processed and ideally raw -omics data in a data repository has become the norm in genomics, transcriptomics and metabolomics, and is frequently required for publication and by grant funders.
However, no repository wide assessment of data quality has ever been carried out.
Our previous experience in working with the Metabolomics Workbench data, as well as in analyzing a variety of transcriptomics and metabolomics datasets, makes us well suited to attempt a repository wide assessment of the analyses available in the Metabolomics Workbench. 

## Methods

6105 analyses were downloaded from the Metabolomics Workbench in November of 2025, as well as any ancillary data files (available as STUDYID_ANALYSISID.txt if present).
Minor repairs to downloaded files were made to make them more amenable to analysis.
The MWTAB JSON file format was used as it made parsing the files easier to implement.

For each analysis, we attempted to:

* convert it to a summarized experiment R object holding metabolite abundances and sample metadata;
* detect if any quality-control samples are included in the sample list;
* evaluate if the data were already log-transformed and needed to be exponentiated;
* count the number of metabolite features and useable samples in each group of subject-sample-factors (SSF);
* calculate information-content-informed Kendall-$\tau$ (ICI-Kt) correlation between all samples;
* calculate the relative standard deviations (RSD) of metabolite features within each SSF group;
* perform principal component analysis (PCA) and calculate an analysis of variance (ANOVA) of the sample principal component scores and SSF groups.

For each of the results of each step, we also attempt to assign a color grade indicating **possible** quality-control and quality-assurance (QC/QA) concerns for a given analysis, providing a score of "red" (think twice before using), "yellow" (probably OK), and "green" (looks good).

## Results

Of the 6103 analyses that could be reasonable parsed, `{r} n_completed` (`{r} perc_display`) were able to go through all the steps to PCA.
Of those xxx had a status of **green** across all the various QC/QA concerns evaluated.
